A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MetaGS work, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A-E. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support matching the equations, algorithm, figures, and tables throughout.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original synthetic and real-world relighting experiments, numerical comparisons, ablations, and qualitative results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain those original experimental results, including quantitative comparisons and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same differentiable Phong model, Gaussian attributes, shadow computation, bilevel meta-learning algorithm, losses, and three-stage training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three synthetic and seven real-world scenes. OOD, camera-light-colocated, environment-map, multi-light, and in-distribution relighting scenarios are retained in Section 4 and Appendix C.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each experiment: NRHints, WildLight, and GS3 for OOD relighting; IRON for colocated relighting; and the same methods in the environment-map experiments and Table 10.

E3.justification: The versions retain the same synthetic 500/100 training/test split, 600 real-world training images per scene, lighting protocols, training budgets, and PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics. Appendix B's rendering and sampling settings also match.

E4.justification: The meta-learning and shadow ablations in Table 3 and Figure 5, larger-batch control in Table 8, and multi-light tests in Figure 8 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-to-run uncertainty. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 2-4 and 6-10 and Figure 8 match, as do the qualitative examples. For example, full-model PSNR remains 27.42 in Table 3, and the real-world average remains 25.83 in Table 7.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1-6, and reasoning in Appendix C.2 and Appendix D are retained. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added, removed, or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about meta-learning, physical shading priors, OOD relighting, and generalization to environment maps.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and interpretation of NRHints' in-distribution advantages are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning complex lighting, direct illumination, subsurface scattering, and anisotropic reflectance.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information match, including PyTorch/Adam, approximately one hour on an RTX 3090, Appendix B's data-generation details, and Table 11's hyperparameters. No code or data access disclosure changes.

R1.justification: Section 5 and all 40 references retain the same cited works and research positioning. No novelty or relationship-to-prior-work claim changes.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2, 27 May 2025, to v3, 16 March 2026, and becomes linked. Apart from spacing differences, the prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-9, Tables 1-11, and Algorithm 1 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement. Embedded figure data match, and rendered pages preserve the layout apart from negligible glyph-rendering differences.

improvement.justification: The main text and Appendices A-E retain the same scientific argument, experimental evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information. The administrative stamp update and negligible typesetting differences do not meaningfully improve or weaken the paper's clarity or evidential support.
